newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY C.BANK SEEN SWINGING TO HUF 58BLN '96 LOSS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY C.BANK SEEN SWINGING TO HUF 58BLN '96 LOSS.

text.p: October figures showed that the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) was likely to post 58 billion loss this year, Gyula Gaal, deputy chairman of the National Assembly's budget committee said on Saturday.
The loss of the NBH increases Hungary's central budget deficit as the central bank's losses are covered by the state.

Gaal was quoted by the daily Nepszabadsag as saying that the NBH would swing to losses from a profit of 6.6 billion forints in 1995 mainly because the NBH paid 113 billion forint interest on state debt in 1996, much more than last year.

The causes of the increase were that the NBH managed a much wider circle of public accounts this year and it had to neutralize the inflationary effects of a large foreign capital inflow by costly money market interventions, Gaal said.
Hungary posted a record privatisation revenue of over $3 billion in 1995, with most of that amount flowing in this year.

The NBH's loss widens the central state budget deficit, while the budget's position will be improved by one-off revenues of 34 billion forints, Finance Ministry Deputy State Secretary Csaba Laszlo said earlier this month.
Laszlo expected the central budget deficit to increase to between 150 and 170 billion forints this year from 111 billion in November, compared with the 1996 target of 233 billion.

The central budget and the social security are the main components of the general government budget, the 1996 deficit of which is forecast at 4.1 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP), as agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
Hungary hopes that the better-than planned position of the central budget will cover the soaring social security deficit.

The social security gap was already 67.3 billion forints in October, compared to the original 1996 target of 17.8 billion, and the 1996 deficit was likely to exceed the 61 billion target in the social security supplementary budget, Laszlo said.
The final amount of the 1996 general government deficit mainly depends on how much revenues of the central budget and the social security will generate in December.
The 1996 GDP product is likely to be around 6600 billion forints.
